findings.title: Sample screenshotRootPath will fail startup unless environment variables are expanded
findings.evidence: Section 13 example: `"screenshotRootPath": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\BSVoiceCAD\\screenshots"`; Section 3: `If EnableStretchEndpoints is true and ScreenshotRootPath is null or does not exist on disk, the viewer throws InvalidOperationException at startup.`
findings.problem: The documented configuration uses a Windows environment-variable token, but bound .NET configuration strings are not expanded automatically. A literal `Directory.Exists("%LOCALAPPDATA%\\BSVoiceCAD\\screenshots")` check will fail.
findings.why_it_matters: Following the spec literally causes startup failure whenever stretch endpoints are enabled, so the documented default configuration is non-functional.
findings.proposed_fix: Require expansion of environment variables before validation, or derive the default path from `Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData)` and document that overrides must be absolute paths.

findings.title: Read-only DI enforcement is not actually specified for an in-process shared host
findings.evidence: `The viewer's DI container resolves only IReadOnlyDhfRepository; no write-capable repository type is registered.` and `ViewerHost.Start(IReadOnlyDhfRepository repo, ViewerOptions options) is called from OrchestratorProgram.Main after DI setup.`
findings.problem: The spec claims DI-based read-only enforcement but never defines a separate viewer service provider. In the same process, starting the viewer after orchestrator DI setup and passing a repo instance directly leaves open that endpoints still share a container where write-capable services are registered.
findings.why_it_matters: The main non-write guarantee can fail at composition time, and the proposed `ViewerReadOnlyDiTests` has no unambiguous target container to verify.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify an isolated viewer composition root/service provider that registers only read-only services, or explicitly require that the shared root provider never registers `IDhfRepository` and define the adapter pattern that preserves read-only access.

findings.title: Deep-validation timeout semantics have no mechanism for partial results
findings.evidence: `Deep validation enforces an 8-second hard timeout via CancellationToken. If the timeout fires, the response is returned with results validated so far and truncated=true.`
findings.problem: A cancellation token normally aborts the operation; it does not by itself produce `entriesChecked`, `lastSequenceChecked`, and partial warnings/failures. The spec does not define a validator or repository contract that can surface progress on cancellation.
findings.why_it_matters: The documented response shape is not implementable or testable as written; implementations will either throw `OperationCanceledException` or return undefined partial state.
findings.proposed_fix: Define `ValidateChainAsync`/validator behavior on cancellation explicitly: return a partial result object, expose incremental checkpoints, or use a progress callback/stream that the endpoint aggregates into the documented response.

findings.title: Entry-detail consistency is falsely assumed rather than specified
findings.evidence: `Entry detail: Single-entry reads are atomic by nature.`
findings.problem: The entry-detail payload in Section 5.2 includes the entry row plus tool calls, decorations, feature trees, and screenshot URLs. That is not automatically atomic unless all related data is read from one transaction/snapshot.
findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent writes can produce mixed-version entry details, undermining auditability and making the viewer show internally inconsistent data.
findings.proposed_fix: Require `GetEntryDetailAsync` to materialize all entry-detail data from a single consistent read transaction/snapshot, or narrow the payload to fields guaranteed by one statement.

findings.title: Entry-detail API contract contradicts itself on feature-tree fields
findings.evidence: Example: `"featureTreeBefore": { "json": "..." }`; field note: `featureTreeBefore | object | yes | SPEC-01 FeatureNode JSON`
findings.problem: The example shows a wrapper object containing a JSON string, while the field table says the field itself is the FeatureNode object. The same contradiction exists for `featureTreeAfter`.
findings.why_it_matters: Clients and tests cannot know whether to expect structured JSON or a serialized blob, so interoperability is undefined.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one representation and make the example, field table, and tests consistent—either inline SPEC-01 FeatureNode JSON or a distinct string field such as `featureTreeBeforeJson`.

findings.title: 503 mapping depends on an undefined exception contract
findings.evidence: `RepositoryUnavailableException is defined in SPEC-04 ... If SPEC-04 does not yet define this type, it wraps NpgsqlException with IsTransient=true or TimeoutException.`
findings.problem: The viewer's outage-handling behavior depends on an exception type that may not exist, and the fallback text does not define a concrete alternative type or detection rule. `wraps NpgsqlException with IsTransient=true` is not a stable contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Different repository implementations can classify the same outage differently, making 503 vs 500 behavior inconsistent and hard to test.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `RepositoryUnavailableException` mandatory in SPEC-04 now, or define a concrete repository-facing error contract/predicate the viewer must use for outage classification.

top_3_must_fix: Expand or replace `%LOCALAPPDATA%` in `screenshotRootPath`; the documented config currently breaks startup.
Define an enforceable isolated read-only composition boundary instead of assuming the shared in-process DI container is safe.
Specify a validator/repository contract that can return partial deep-validation results on timeout.
